Tashakour completes the shortlist. [Adrian Wall]

6.45.spotlight_verdict: A wide-open maiden. Of those with form in the book, Enceladus, Theorist and Trojan Fighter have shown enough to make the shortlist but the vote goes to REYNIR, a nicely bred colt who lost all chance at the start at Gowran on debut and is worth another chance. Sporting the same colours, any market support for Dermot Weld's Almazann could be significant. [Adrian Wall]

7.15.betting_forecast: 13/8 Limestone, 9/4 Port Ferdinand, 7/2 Mr Vettori, 9/2 Summer Is Tomorrow.
7.15.spotlight_verdict: A small turnout but a very interesting race in which cases for all four runners can be made, all making their seasonal return. Three of these hold Derby entries, slight preference at this moment in time is for LIMESTONE, whose yard is in excellent form and with whom Joey Sheridan has struck up a profitable partnership this season. Port Ferdinand is the least exposed and has to be respected, while Mr Vettori is another who should improve for this step up in trip. [Alan Hewison]

Final Voyage 8 9-1 J Murtagh Jessica Maye (7) 12-1 85 86 102 Seven-time winner, last win at Dundalk in February 2024 off 3lb higher; some good efforts last year, including over this trip on the AW, and creditable run in the circumstances (slowly away) at the Curragh on latest under today's rider; one to consider. Quatre Bras 5 9-1 R O'Brien Reese Holohan (7) 13-2 85 70 101 Three-time AW winner (twice at 1m2f); out of form on turf last season but some good runs this term, good second over inadequate 7f at Naas (soft) and nine days ago at Leopardstown when coming late to dead-heat for fourth with Amplitude over this trip, having not had the clearest of runs; better ground here to suit and has to be on the shortlist with rider now claiming 7lb. Ben Lawers 4 8-13t Mrs J Harrington Keithen Kennedy (5) 14-1 83 69 103 Off the mark in 1m AW maiden at Dundalk in February and beaten under 2l in valuable Lingfield AW handicap early this month over same trip; barely gets 1m2f so potentially vulnerable back on the turf. Page 8 spotlightcork 24.04.26 Calm The Jets 4 8-13 C Farrell Rory Cleary 12-1 83 77 94 Landed a 1m maiden at Dundalk on debut impressively in January 2024; off the track (gelded) until never landing a blow in midfield in quite valuable Curragh handicap over same trip early this month (2l off Final Voyage, ahead of Iron Fist); entitled to come on for that and remains unexposed on only third career start and upped in trip. Amplitude 4 8-12 Joseph G Murphy Gary Carroll 7-1 82 - 99 Rounded off last term in with emphatic win in 9.5f Gowran maiden (heavy) and similar level of form on second start back when dead-heating for fourth with Quatre Bras in Leopardstown handicap over this trip nine days ago; respected. Eben Zaabeel 5 8-9 A Martin N G McCullagh 25-1 79 - 99 Seven-race maiden in Britain for Charlie Hills, runner-up in AW handicaps final two starts; never sighted on hurdles debut at Fairyhouse early this month, probably best watched for now.

Following a fine recent comeback run at the Curragh, BAY COLONY could be the one to side with here, even though she probably wants a bit further. Nothing separated Quatre Bras and Amplitude at Leopardstown but the former now has a valuable 7lb claimed and could emerge the main threat. Topweight Defiantly has to be respected dropped in grade, while Apercu and Mano Chicago are others to consider. [Alan Hewison] Page 9 spotlightcork 24.04.26
